name: cbs-wijken-en-buurten
title: CBS Wijken en Buurten (Neighborhoods and Districts with Demographics)
description: The definitive Dutch demographic geodataset. Published annually by CBS (Statistics Netherlands), this dataset provides demographic, socioeconomic, and geographic statistics at three nested administrative levels: buurten (neighborhoods), wijken (districts), and gemeenten (municipalities). It is the primary source for neighborhood-level population, age, household, migration background, and urbanity data across the entire Netherlands.

provider.name: CBS (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / Statistics Netherlands)
provider.description: The Dutch national statistics office, responsible for collecting and publishing statistical data about the Netherlands.

crs.name: Amersfoort / RD New
crs.note: The standard Dutch national coordinate reference system (Rijksdriehoekstelsel). Convert to EPSG:4326 (WGS 84) for web mapping or GeoParquet.

coverage: Netherlands (all land and water areas, including a 'Buitenland' boundary marker entry)

temporal.reference_date: Statistics reflect the situation as of 1 January of the publication year.

hierarchy.description: The three layers form a strict spatial hierarchy. Each buurt belongs to exactly one wijk, and each wijk belongs to exactly one gemeente. The code system encodes this relationship.

levels.description: Top-level administrative unit. The Netherlands had 342 municipalities as of 1 Jan 2025, but the dataset includes additional entries (424 total) for historical/special cases.
Mid-level statistical unit. Each wijk aggregates one or more buurten and belongs to one gemeente. The first 4 digits after WK match the gemeente code.
Finest-grained statistical unit. The first 6 digits after BU encode the wijk (and implicitly the gemeente). 14,823 features total, of which ~14,230 carry actual demographic data.

code_system.description: CBS area codes embed the hierarchy. For buurtcode BU00140000: GM=0014 (gemeente Groningen), WK=001400 (wijk 00 within Groningen), BU=00140000 (buurt 0000 within that wijk).
code_system.gemeente_from_buurt: Take characters 3-6 of buurtcode (0-indexed: 2:6) to get the 4-digit gemeente code.
code_system.wijk_from_buurt: Take characters 3-8 of buurtcode (0-indexed: 2:8) to get the 6-digit wijk code.

reasons: Privacy protection: areas with too few residents (typically <50) have statistics suppressed to prevent identification of individuals.
Not applicable: water-only areas and the 'Buitenland' (foreign territory) boundary marker have no meaningful demographic data.
Data not collected: some statistics may not be available for certain areas.
-99997.affected_columns: All numeric statistical columns (population, percentages, densities, household counts, area measurements).
-99997.handling_advice: Filter out -99997 values before computing averages, sums, or other aggregations. In SQL: WHERE aantal_inwoners != -99997. In Python/pandas: df.replace(-99997, pd.NA).

buitenland.description: A boundary marker entry labeled 'Buitenland' (Foreign) present in each layer. All statistical values are -99997. Represents the area outside the Netherlands.
buitenland.handling: Exclude from analysis. Filter by: WHERE buurtnaam != 'Buitenland' or WHERE aantal_inwoners != -99997.

water_areas.description: Areas where the 'water' column is 'JA' represent water bodies (seas, lakes, major rivers). These typically have suppressed demographic statistics.
water_areas.handling: Filter by: WHERE water = 'NEE' for land-based analysis.

buurten.name: buurten
buurten.description: Finest-grained statistical areas. Each buurt is a small neighborhood within a gemeente, typically containing a few hundred to a few thousand residents.

wijken.name: wijken
wijken.description: Mid-level aggregation of buurten into districts. Each wijk belongs to one gemeente.

gemeenten.name: gemeenten
gemeenten.feature_count_note: More than the 342 current municipalities — includes historical/special entries.
gemeenten.description: Top-level administrative units (municipalities). Each gemeente aggregates all wijken and buurten within its boundary.

schema.description: All three layers share the same column schema (with minor naming differences for the area code/name columns). The columns below use the buurten naming convention; wijken use wijkcode/wijknaam, gemeenten use gemeentecode/gemeentenaam.

columns.name: buurtcode
columns.description: CBS identifier with prefix BU (buurt), WK (wijk), or GM (gemeente) followed by numeric digits. Encodes the hierarchical relationship between levels.

columns.name: buurtnaam
columns.description: Human-readable name of the area.

columns.name: wijkcode
columns.description: The wijk (district) that this buurt belongs to. Format: WK + 6 digits.

columns.name: gemeentecode
columns.description: The gemeente this area belongs to. Format: GM + 4 digits. Present on buurten and wijken layers.

columns.name: gemeentenaam
columns.description: Human-readable name of the parent municipality.

columns.name: indelingswijziging_wijken_en_buurten
columns.description: Whether this area's boundaries changed compared to the previous year. 1 = boundaries changed, 0 = unchanged. Useful for time-series analysis to identify areas that cannot be directly compared year-over-year.

columns.name: water
columns.description: Whether this area is primarily a water body. 'JA' = water area (seas, lakes, major rivers), 'NEE' = land area. Water areas typically have all demographic statistics suppressed (-99997).

columns.name: meest_voorkomende_postcode
columns.description: The dominant 4-digit postal code (PC4) in this area. Based on address counts. Useful for joining with postal-code-based datasets.

columns.name: dekkingspercentage
columns.description: Percentage of addresses in this area that fall within the most common postal code. Higher values indicate the area aligns well with the postal code; lower values indicate the area spans multiple postal codes.

columns.name: omgevingsadressendichtheid
columns.description: Average number of addresses within a 1 km radius of each address in the area. A measure of local urbanization intensity. Higher values indicate denser, more urban environments.

columns.name: stedelijkheid_adressen_per_km2
columns.description: CBS urbanity classification on a 1-5 scale based on surrounding address density. Derived from omgevingsadressendichtheid.

values.1: Zeer sterk stedelijk / Very highly urban (>=2500 addresses/km2)

columns.name: bevolkingsdichtheid_inwoners_per_km2
columns.description: Number of residents per square kilometer of land area.

columns.name: aantal_inwoners
columns.description: Total population registered in the area.

columns.name: mannen
columns.description: Number of male residents.

columns.name: vrouwen
columns.description: Number of female residents.

columns.name: percentage_personen_0_tot_15_jaar
columns.description: Percentage of the population aged 0 to 14 years (children).

columns.name: percentage_personen_15_tot_25_jaar
columns.description: Percentage of the population aged 15 to 24 years (young adults, students).

columns.name: percentage_personen_25_tot_45_jaar
columns.description: Percentage of the population aged 25 to 44 years (young working age).

columns.name: percentage_personen_45_tot_65_jaar
columns.description: Percentage of the population aged 45 to 64 years (older working age).

columns.name: percentage_personen_65_jaar_en_ouder
columns.description: Percentage of the population aged 65 and older (elderly/retired).

columns.name: percentage_ongehuwd
columns.description: Percentage of the population that has never been married.

columns.name: percentage_gehuwd
columns.description: Percentage of the population currently married (including registered partnerships).

columns.name: percentage_gescheid
columns.description: Percentage of the population that is divorced.

columns.name: percentage_verweduwd
columns.description: Percentage of the population that is widowed.

columns.name: aantal_huishoudens
columns.description: Total number of private households in the area.

columns.name: percentage_eenpersoonshuishoudens
columns.description: Percentage of households consisting of one person living alone.

columns.name: percentage_huishoudens_zonder_kinderen
columns.description: Percentage of multi-person households without children.

columns.name: percentage_huishoudens_met_kinderen
columns.description: Percentage of households with one or more children.

columns.name: gemiddelde_huishoudsgrootte
columns.description: Average number of persons per household. Low values (1.0-1.5) indicate student/single neighborhoods; higher values (3.0+) indicate family areas.

columns.name: percentage_met_herkomstland_nederland
columns.description: Percentage of the population with a Dutch migration background (herkomstland). Under CBS definition: both parents were born in the Netherlands.

columns.name: percentage_met_herkomstland_uit_europa_excl_nl
columns.dutch: Percentage met herkomstland uit Europa (excl. NL)
columns.description: Percentage of the population with a migration background from another European country. Includes both first and second generation.

columns.name: percentage_met_herkomstland_buiten_europa
columns.description: Percentage of the population with a migration background from outside Europe. Includes both first and second generation.

columns.name: percentage_geb_in_nl_met_herkomstland_nederland
columns.dutch: Percentage geboren in NL met herkomstland Nederland
columns.english: % born in NL with Dutch background
columns.description: Percentage born in the Netherlands with both parents also born in the Netherlands. Represents the 'native Dutch' population in the CBS definition.

columns.name: perc_geb_in_nl_met_herkomstland_in_europa_ex_nl
columns.dutch: Percentage geboren in NL met herkomstland in Europa (excl. NL)
columns.english: % born in NL with European background
columns.description: Second-generation European migration background: born in the Netherlands but with at least one parent born in another European country.

columns.name: perc_geb_in_nl_met_herkomstland_buiten_europa
columns.dutch: Percentage geboren in NL met herkomstland buiten Europa
columns.english: % born in NL with non-European background
columns.description: Second-generation non-European migration background: born in the Netherlands but with at least one parent born outside Europe.

columns.name: perc_geb_buiten_nl_met_herkomstlnd_in_europa_ex_nl
columns.dutch: Percentage geboren buiten NL met herkomstland in Europa (excl. NL)
columns.description: First-generation European immigrants: born in another European country.

columns.name: perc_geb_buiten_nl_met_herkomstlnd_buiten_europa
columns.dutch: Percentage geboren buiten NL met herkomstland buiten Europa
columns.description: First-generation non-European immigrants: born outside Europe.

columns.name: oppervlakte_totaal_in_ha
columns.description: Total surface area of the region in hectares (1 ha = 10,000 m2). Includes both land and water.

columns.name: oppervlakte_land_in_ha
columns.description: Land surface area in hectares. Used as the denominator for population density calculations.

columns.name: oppervlakte_water_in_ha
columns.description: Water surface area in hectares.

columns.name: jrstatcode
columns.description: Composite key combining the year and the area code, e.g., '2025BU00140000'. Useful for multi-year datasets to create unique identifiers.

columns.name: jaar
columns.description: The reference year for the statistics (e.g., 2025). All records in a single file share the same year.

sample_data.note: Classic university-town neighborhood: very high youth percentage, dominated by single-person households.

cbs_gebiedsindelingen.description: CBS Gebiedsindelingen (Area Classifications) provides boundary geometries without demographic data. Use Wijken en Buurten when you need statistics; use Gebiedsindelingen when you only need boundaries or need additional geographic levels (COROP, provinces, labor market regions).

bestuurlijke_gebieden.description: Kadaster Bestuurlijke Gebieden provides the authoritative administrative boundaries for municipalities, provinces, and national territory. CBS boundaries are derived from these but may differ slightly due to statistical rounding.

bag.description: Basisregistratie Adressen en Gebouwen (BAG) contains individual address and building data. Can be aggregated to buurt level for more detailed analysis.

notes: This is THE go-to dataset for any neighborhood-level demographic analysis in the Netherlands. It combines statistical data from CBS with geographic boundaries, enabling spatial analysis of population, housing, and migration patterns at the finest available granularity.
All percentage columns are integers (rounded to whole numbers), not decimals.
The five age-group percentages should sum to approximately 100 for valid areas.
The three migration-background percentages (Dutch, European, non-European) should sum to approximately 100.
The three marital-status percentages (unmarried, married, divorced, widowed) should sum to approximately 100.
Population density is calculated using land area only (oppervlakte_land_in_ha), excluding water.

Municipal mergers happen regularly in the Netherlands (several per year). When municipalities merge, all their buurten and wijken are renumbered. The indelingswijziging column helps track these changes.
